title: 1:1 SEN Learning Facilitator
summary: Give personalised learning and emotional support to primary-aged pupils with SEMH, autism and speech and language needs.
body:
## The position

We're working with a specialist provision in Witham to recruit a dedicated one-to-one SEN learning facilitator. It's an excellent opportunity to support primary-aged pupils with complex SEMH, autism and speech and language needs in a nurturing, structured and therapeutic environment.

This bespoke provision delivers a creative sensory curriculum that helps pupils develop socially, emotionally and academically, building confidence, independence and positive engagement with learning.

Working closely with the class teacher, you'll provide personalised learning and emotional support, and play a key role in helping pupils reach their full potential.

## The role

### Supporting pupils

- Build positive, trusting relationships that promote self-esteem and independence.
- Provide tailored support for pupils' social, emotional and mental health needs.
- Adapt communication to individual learning styles and needs.
- Support behaviour management in line with school policies.
- Help implement individual education and support plans.

### Teaching and learning support

- Support the delivery of differentiated learning activities.
- Help pupils access a broad and balanced curriculum.
- Give teachers feedback on pupil progress and development.
- Monitor, record and report on engagement and attainment.
- Help maintain a safe, structured and positive learning environment.

### Teamwork and safeguarding

- Work closely with teachers, therapists and other professionals.
- Support communication with parents and carers where appropriate.
- Contribute positively to the wider school community.
- Promote and safeguard the welfare of all pupils, following child protection procedures at all times.

## What you'll need

### Essential

- GCSE English and Maths (grade 4/C or above) or equivalent.
- Experience working with children or young people.
- An understanding of SEN, particularly SEMH and/or autism.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- A calm, patient and resilient approach.

### Desirable

- Experience in a school or specialist provision.
- Experience supporting pupils with SEMH and/or autism.
- Experience in a primary setting.

### Personal qualities

- A passion for supporting children with additional needs.
- A positive, proactive and resilient mindset.
- A commitment to safeguarding and inclusion.
- A strong team player.

## Benefits

- Term-time only contract.
- Company pension scheme.
- Specialist training, including Thrive, safeguarding and Essex Steps.
- Free onsite parking.
- Free uniform.
- Option of free lunches.
- Ongoing support from Bright Futures throughout the recruitment process.
